entities.name: virtual private network
entities.label: Idea
entities.summary:
A Virtual Private Network (VPN) is a foundational networking technology that securely extends a private network across a public network, such as the internet, making it appear to users as if their computing device were directly connected to the private network. Emerging in the mid-1990s as the internet gained commercial traction, VPNs fundamentally transformed how businesses and individuals accessed remote resources and protected their digital communications. They allowed for the secure transmission of sensitive data over inherently insecure public infrastructure, becoming indispensable for corporate telecommuting, inter-office connectivity, and later, individual privacy and circumvention of geo-restrictions.

The conceptual groundwork for VPNs, particularly secure tunnels, existed earlier, but the practical implementation gained momentum with Microsoft's development of the Point-to-Point Tunneling Protocol (PPTP) in 1996. This protocol enabled the encapsulation of network packets for secure transmission over IP networks. Subsequent advancements saw the development of more robust and secure protocols like Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol (L2TP/IPsec) and OpenVPN, the latter released as open-source software in 2001, quickly becoming an industry standard due to its flexibility and strong encryption. These technologies facilitated the widespread adoption of remote work models, enabling employees to securely access internal company servers from any internet-connected location, thus decentralizing the traditional office environment.
